results.title: Zeroing 1,000 loop neurons cuts loops but not errors
results.what: Turning off 1,000 neurons (0.28 %) linked to repetition loops in the cued base cut looping answers from 71 to 19 and tokens per problem by 17 %. Right answers moved only from 378 to 381 of 500.

studies.about: how much the meta-review layer improves the research

results.title: The opening cue takes the base from 45 % to 82 %
results.what: On MATH-500 at temperature 1.0, the untrained base model gets 224 of 500 right from the plain prompt and 410 of 500 when its answer is started with a three-token cue copied from the RL-trained model's answers.

results.title: Temperature does not change the RL model's score
results.what: The RL model with a plain prompt scored 463/500 at temperature 1.0 and 464/500 at 0.6, a difference of -0.2 points (interval -1.8 to 1.4).

results.title: At T 0.6 the cued base loops, and restarts recover it
results.what: At T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 the base with cue gets 354 of 500, with 119 cap hits. Restarting each cap hit, up to two more times, and scoring the first attempt that finishes gives 414. The RL model gets 464 at T 0.6.
sc: cue, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, restart cap hits up to 3 times

results.title: Base without the cue scores 61 to 64 % at temperature 0.6
results.what: With a plain prompt at temperature 0.6, the base scored 319/500 and 305/500 in two runs under grader v3. The older 57.2 % figure came from the stricter grader v1.

results.title: On 328 harder problems RL leads the cued base by 13 points
results.what: Both models answer 328 harder problems, all absent from the RL training set, once each at temperature 1.0. The base with cue gets 164 (50.0 %) and the RL model 206 (62.8 %), at equal tokens per problem (9,345 and 9,316).

results.title: Cued base at temperature 0.6 without a top-p cut: 378/500
results.what: At temperature 0.6 with no top-p cut, the cued base scored 378/500 (75.6 %): 4.8 points above top-p 0.95 and 6.4 points below temperature 1.0.

results.title: Hard-set scores at temperature 1.0 for base and RL
results.what: On the 328 harder problems at temperature 1.0: base 76 plain and 164 with the cue, RL 206 plain and 205 with the cue. Raising temperature from 0.6 to 1.0 adds 13.7 points to the cued base.

results.title: On 328 hard problems, RL leads the cued base by 12.8 points
results.what: On 328 harder problems at temperature 1.0, RL scored 206 and the base with the cue 164. At temperature 0.6 the gap was 25.9 points, with the cued base at 119.

results.title: A quarter of the RL weight change gives most of the gain
results.what: Adding a fraction of the RL-minus-base weight change to the base: with the cue, a quarter scores 441/500 against 410, and more stays at 450 to 457. A random change of equal size scores 417; the Code-RL change 450.
sc: base + random matched-norm difference, cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0

results.title: Cutting the sampling tail does not help at temperature 1
results.what: Min-p and top-p truncation at temperature 1.0 scored 404 to 412 of 500 for the cued base, within noise of untruncated sampling (410). RL moved by +0.6 points.

results.title: A vote over 4 samples lifts the base to 89 %, RL still leads
results.what: At T 1.0, both models answer each MATH-500 problem 4 times. The vote takes the base with cue from 405 to 446 of 500 and the RL model from 456 to 474. Restarting cap hits adds 8 problems alone and 4 on top of the vote.
